claims.statement: ECHA states that all hazardous mixtures in scope require a UFI and that a product must not be placed on the market until the UFI is included in a valid poison-centre notification.
ECHA states that each UFI corresponds to one mixture composition and uses an internal formulation number in its generation.
The harmonised PCN information includes the full mixture composition, covering hazardous and non-hazardous components.

contrary_evidence: Only hazardous mixtures within scope need this workflow; non-hazardous portfolios do not create the same gate.
ECHA supplies a UFI generator and submission ecosystem, limiting willingness to pay for generation alone.
A supplier can withhold full composition and instead provide MiM identifiers, making end-to-end formula lineage incomplete.

economics.acquisition_route: Partner with two SDS/CLP consultants, pilot on a redacted or sandbox portfolio, and use label-to-UFI preflight as a lead tool
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated 5-7 year scenario: 120 customers averaging 45,000 PLN annual revenue yields 5.4m PLN; at 35% EBITDA, 4x, and 75% ownership, equity value is about 5.67m PLN.
economics.founder_time: 18-24 hours per week, with chemistry/regulatory sign-off from contracted specialists and security design treated as a core deliverable
economics.gross_margin_basis: Data transformations and consistency checks are repeatable; expert CLP review, translation, and incomplete supplier data are variable-cost drivers
economics.payback: Customer payback hypothesis: avoiding rework across labels, SDS files, and national products can recover a 20,000-60,000 PLN annual cost for multi-SKU portfolios; validate against consultant spend
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: 5,000-20,000 PLN secure onboarding, 2,000-7,000 PLN per new or materially changed formula, and 1,500-5,000 PLN monthly portfolio monitoring
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every formula, supplier, label, language, product-name, and market change touches the same confidential record and can require notification updates

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A customer-specific formula and supplier lineage graph plus validated exception rules makes every later variant and update faster while increasing migration cost
fingerprint.customer: Small EU formulators, importers, and private-label operators of hazardous cleaning, coating, adhesive, and maintenance mixtures
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Chemical regulatory consultants, SDS authors, contract manufacturers, packaging/label agencies, and private-label trade groups
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Encrypted formula vault, UFI/formula mapping, label/SDS reconciliation, PCN dataset generation, approvals, and update alerts; hypothesis 2,000-7,000 PLN per formula plus 1,500-5,000 PLN monthly portfolio fee
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Regulatory or product-development lead pays secure onboarding, per-formula preparation, and annual vault/change-monitoring fees
fingerprint.problem_trigger: New formulation or private-label SKU, composition/supplier change, new member-state market, label revision, or rejected PCN submission

founder_fit: Strong data-lineage and validation fit with FMCG familiarity, without assuming use of employer IP
Partner-led B2B distribution reduces continuous social selling
Can start as a tightly scoped secure workflow before automating submission formats
Requires explicit conflict-of-interest review and strict avoidance of Reckitt data, formulations, vendors, or work time
risks: A formula breach would be catastrophic; security and isolation costs may exceed the starting budget
Chemical classification errors can harm users and create liability
ECHA tools and established regulatory consultants may be sufficient for small portfolios
Employer conflict or perceived competitive overlap could make this opportunity unsuitable

structure.commercial_archetype: Confidential formulation vault with per-formula notification operations and recurring change-control subscription
structure.control_point: The formula-version release record proving that the UFI printed on the product is linked to a valid poison-centre notification
structure.critical_dependency: Complete and accurate composition/MiM data from formulators and suppliers, secure handling of trade secrets, and valid ECHA submission identities/formats

thesis: Planning-stage hypothesis: offer a secure formula-to-market release workflow for small EU makers and importers of detergents, cleaners, adhesives, coatings, and other hazardous mixtures. It would maintain confidential composition and mixture-in-mixture lineage, generate and bind each UFI to the correct formulation, assemble harmonised Poison Centre Notification data, reconcile labels/SDS/product names, and trigger updates when composition or market coverage changes. A SKU cannot leave the client's internal release queue until the UFI is linked to a valid notification. Because formula history is sensitive and costly to reconstruct, secure custody and deterministic change control can create unusually strong retention if trust is earned.
